units.text: The Emancipation Proclamation was issued by Abraham Lincoln on January 1, 1863. Multiple sources confirm the date and Lincoln as the issuer.

citations.title: Introduction - Emancipation Proclamation: Primary Documents in American History - Research Guides at Library of Congress
Introduction - Emancipation Proclamation: Primary Documents in American History - Research Guides at Library of Congress

judgement.reason: The passages support that Abraham Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation on January 1, 1863, but the provided passages are two identical entries from the same source, so they do not support the claim of multiple sources confirming it.

units.text: The Proclamation text itself declares it was 'Done at the City of Washington this first day of January', confirming the location as Washington, D.C.

Emancipation Proclamation | Abraham Lincoln Presidential Library and Museum

judgement.reason: The passage quotes the Proclamation as saying 'Done at the City of Washington this first day of January', directly supporting the quoted wording and identifying the location as the City of Washington (Washington, D.C.).

units.text: Spans from the National Archives Prologue Magazine (1993) confirm Lincoln signed the Emancipation Proclamation on January 1, 1863, at the White House in the nation's capital.

judgement.reason: The passages confirm January 1, 1863, in the nation's capital and that the document was brought to the White House, but they do not state that Lincoln signed it there.
